verdict.rationale: Docs detail fine-grained permission controls (permission modes, canUseTool callback), hooks that can block dangerous shell/file operations, subagents with independent tool access/permissions, and admin-level MCP restrictions, plus hosting guidance covering Docker/Kubernetes/sandbox providers and multi-tenant isolation for production deployment. This directly matches both the tool-permission and sandboxed-execution parts of the story with first-party depth. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on validation that sandbox isolation and permission enforcement hold up in adversarial real-world use, and more concrete sandbox-provider implementation detail beyond a mention.
